custody/intent.rs submit path: seed load failure or a non-BadRequest prepare error rejects the prepared row best-effort; if that UPDATE fails the account stays blocked by uq_custodial_intent_one_inflight until the 120s abandon sweep. Attack: a prepared row that never arms and a sweep that is not running.

record_settlement on the handler path: a transaction-row INSERT failure returns 202 status=submitted and relies on the sweep (600s after arm) to settle by hash; the ledger row is late by up to ~10 minutes in that case (by design, never a 200 with btxid:null).
resume: the ambiguous-count gate is a separate SELECT before RESUME_SQL (TOCTOU window between the count and the UPDATE); mitigated by being admin-only with an explicit force flag.

Reconciliation All-scope walk under RECONCILIATION_MAX_ACCOUNTS/DEADLINE reads every custodial address from Horizon at concurrency 8 inside the daily job and POST /admin/reconciliation/snapshots (the latter under the 30s request timeout — a large fleet makes the manual snapshot time out at the HTTP layer while the handler continues; the row is still recorded). obligations.cycle_holds_minor is a journal net over cycle-linked entries (SUM held_delta), which is exact but differs from the spec's prose.

chk_cpi_hash_state + uq_custodial_intent_hash: a definitively rejected envelope keeps its hash forever, so the same signed envelope can never be re-armed by a new intent (intended: a new sequence produces a new hash).
Existing ReserveRefundListQuery uses #[serde(flatten)] PaginationParams which serde_urlencoded cannot parse for numeric fields (`?page=2` likely 400s) — pre-existing, not in this lane's scope.
UI reserve.js swallows a failed positions fetch (no drift badge); the Custody page surfaces the error instead. custody.js gates the Resume button on manage_roles as the admin proxy.
